papers.title: Replacing Large Language Models with Jev Decision Models for Low-Latency Edge Service Orchestration
papers.problem: Apps that ask a language model to read each request wait too long, so requests miss their time limit.
papers.fix: A small decision model cut median decision time by 22.7-64.5% against the fastest language model, across 33 test conditions.
papers.practicalUseCase: If speed matters more than flexibility, swap the big model for a decision model on fixed-format requests.
papers.limitation: It works for requests with a few fixed fields; wide formats mark the limit of the swap.

papers.title: Ego2Act: Evaluating Goal-Directed Manipulation in Egocentric Video Generation
papers.problem: Video generators claim to simulate the real world, but no test checked whether they finish multi-step tasks.
papers.fix: Tested on 2,640 videos, models often skip or half-do steps and fail at fine physical detail.
papers.practicalUseCase: Do not trust generated videos as a plan for real actions, because later steps often lack the needed setup.
papers.limitation: The benchmark covers 110 everyday hand tasks, so other kinds of tasks may behave differently.

papers.title: MemFold: Learning Compact Soft Memory for Long-Context Personalization via On-Policy Optimization
papers.problem: Assistants that remember one user for long either keep growing text or squeeze memory in ways that ignore real use.
papers.fix: MemFold, a fixed-size memory trained on its own answers, scored highest on PersonaMem-32K and PersonaMem-128K, widening on longer histories.
papers.practicalUseCase: Train memory by how well answers come out, not by how well it copies text, and keep memory size fixed.
papers.limitation: Results come from three Qwen models and a few benchmarks, so other model families remain untested.

papers.title: Persona Dosing: Calibrated Activation Steering for Graded Trait Control
papers.problem: Steering a language model gives no dial for how strongly a persona trait shows up in answers.
papers.fix: PersonaDose raised trait strength by 33.2, 18.3, and 17.8 points over a common method, with 4.7-6.2 points target error.
papers.practicalUseCase: You can request a trait at a set strength, but only within the range the controller learned.
papers.limitation: Only 14-22 of 28 target strengths were reachable per model, and coherence dropped for some traits on new questions.

papers.title: Sustainability Committees and Environmental Initiatives: Insights from Dual Banking Systems in Emerging Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Banks form sustainability committees, but nobody knew if those committees change environmental results at Islamic banks.
papers.fix: Committees link to better environmental scores, but at Islamic banks they lift only overall and resource-reduction scores, not products.
papers.practicalUseCase: A committee at an Islamic bank may signal intent more than real change, so check for green products.
papers.limitation: The study shows links in emerging markets, not proof of cause, and the Islamic bank group shows weaker effects.

papers.title: Trends and Determinants of Sustainability Sukuk Issuance: Evidence from Global Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Sustainability sukuk are growing fast, yet little was known about what drives how large each issue is.
papers.fix: In 11,944 sukuk issues from 2012 to 2022, equity-based contracts, better security, and longer debt terms link to larger issues.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you plan an issue, use equity-based contracts and keep second-party opinion costs low, since higher costs shrink issue size.
papers.limitation: Data end in 2022, and the results show links between factors and size, not cause.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence and Big Data Strategies to Enhance Islamic Banks’ Competitiveness and Sustainable Development
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Islamic banks in Jordan add AI and big data, but the effect on competitiveness and sustainability was unclear.
papers.fix: AI use, data analytics, and data management link positively to competitiveness and sustainability; staff digital skill helps only competitiveness.
papers.practicalUseCase: Spend on AI and data systems first, since staff digital training alone did not lift sustainable performance.
papers.limitation: The survey covers 214 managers at 15 Jordanian banks at one point in time, so it shows links, not cause.

papers.title: ICT, High-Tech Exports, and Institutions as Drivers of Bank Expansion Growth in a Dual Banking System
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Nobody knew which factors drive growth for Islamic and conventional banks side by side.
papers.fix: In 218 banks across 12 countries, ICT adoption drives growth most, and high-tech exports help only alongside ICT.
papers.practicalUseCase: Digital investment pays off most where national innovation is strong, so invest in both together.
papers.limitation: The sample covers 12 countries, and Islamic banks depend more on governance quality than conventional banks.

papers.title: Determinants of Financial Inclusion in the OIC and OECD Countries: Are They Different?
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.institution: International Centre for Education in Islamic Finance
papers.problem: Many Muslim-majority countries still exclude people from financial services, even though Islamic finance has grown for a decade.
papers.fix: In 35 countries from 2005 to 2021, income, schooling, institutions, and internet access drive financial inclusion in OIC countries.
papers.practicalUseCase: OIC countries must invest in digital networks, youth and women, and income to include more people.
papers.limitation: The data cover 35 countries and show links, not cause.

papers.title: Global prevalence of impostor phenomenon in medical students: A systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.institution: National University Toribio Rodríguez de Mendoza
papers.problem: Medical students face constant exams and peer comparison, and nobody had pooled how often they feel like impostors.
papers.fix: Impostor feelings were frequent among pre-licensure medical students worldwide.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you feel like a fraud while training hard, know it is common, and seek support early.
papers.limitation: Results vary a lot between studies, and rates depend on how students were sampled and where.

papers.title: Psychometric properties of the Arabic Perceived Digital Well-Being Scale (PDWS) in Saudi young adults
papers.institution: Imam Mohammad ibn Saud Islamic University
papers.problem: Most phone-use research measures risk and addiction, so no Arabic tool measured how people judge their own digital life.
papers.fix: The Arabic scale showed a clear three-part structure, and higher scores matched more life satisfaction and less missing-out fear.
papers.practicalUseCase: You can now measure whether phone use helps or hurts Saudi young adults, instead of counting hours online.
papers.limitation: Participants were self-selected online volunteers aged 18-25 from Riyadh, and the design shows links, not cause.
